title: The Cost of Learning Under Multiple Change Points

split.decision: Online real NAB CPU streams; no offline training. Development: first three lexicographically sorted non-target ec2_cpu_utilization series in NAB realAWSCloudwatch, 12096 observations; public master 20261030; NAB annotated event timestamps delimit sample-mean reference segments. Evaluation: unchanged complete released-code stream and original manual reference segmentation held by the judge. Development/evaluation source series, episode seeds and ids are disjoint. Current observation is allowed; future observations are forbidden. Seeds identify episodes only; raw observations are materialized and never generated from seeds.

baseline.timing_scope: legacy protocol estimates retained for operational budgeting; not a measured v2 reference

allowed_changes: Online mean estimators, change-point detectors, working noise/latent-state approximations, auxiliary training losses, optimizers and numerical methods may change.
ATC, its sigma1/alpha.05 tuning and exact scan implementation are baseline choices; the evaluation squared loss and reference segmentation are not candidate-selectable.
When retaining the supplied ATC pipeline, changing only sigma=1, alpha=0.05, the `gamma_paper` coefficients 6 and 2, or a global multiplier on that threshold does not count as a method improvement.
fixed_contract: Track the fixed reference segment mean of each NAB CPU stream using the original experiment observation order, minimizing mean endpoint cumulative squared error.
Original stream observations, episode horizons/boundaries and fixed reference segment means are the research objects; candidate detection rules cannot relabel the evaluation target.

At step t, observe X_t then submit an estimate using X_1:t before observing X_(t+1); each episode has fresh state. The original experiment metric sums squared errors at all released timestamps and averages episode endpoints.
Supplied data/splits, evaluation metric, trusted evaluator and lawful information access.
method_freedom_review.budget_policy: agent overall deadline; separate overall formal replay budget
forbidden_substitutions: Do not replace current segment-mean tracking with next-observation prediction or retrospective smoothing, redefine change points/means in labels, or optimize a substituted reference.
No future observations, hidden means, precomputed episode estimates, seed reconstruction or state/data reuse from another evaluation episode.
Training or fitting reusable model state or learned preprocessing on validation features or labels, including final train+val refits or validation-based distillation.

evidence.finding: Scientific object is piecewise-stationary mean tracking with squared-error regret. The theoretical formulation uses F_(t-1), whereas the selected released NAB experiment includes the current observation.
Original experiment hatmu[t]=(cs[t]-cs[r])/(t-r), including X_t; current-sample alarms set hatmu[t]=X[t-1].
NAB experiment sums (res[hatmu]-mu_t)^2 at the same timestamps; no shift to one-step-ahead prediction.
Private state machine owns the observe/submit sequence and only returns completed trusted records.
Reconstructs squared errors against fixed reference means and averages endpoint sums.

research_contract_review.verification_scope: Task-specific research-scope review and bounded checks; not a new performance/readiness certification.

validation_policy.learned_preprocessing: fit on training only; apply frozen fitted transforms to validation/test
validation_policy.instance_roles: Preserve explicit per-instance observation/training/calibration/causal-feedback roles; no evaluation-target fitting or validation-derived fitted state carried across independent cases.
validation_policy.enforcement: binding prompt and task contract; task-specific replay/guards where available; arbitrary training-data provenance requires source/patch audit
